subject: Human Evolution
title: Back-Migrations
description: A fast breakdown of Back-Migrations for builders.

hook.text: The out-of-Africa story isn't one-way. DNA shows multiple waves of people migrating back into Africa.

buildup.text: Eurasian populations carrying Neanderthal DNA moved back into North and East Africa over millennia.

discovery.text: This is why some African populations carry small amounts of Neanderthal DNA—it arrived via back-migration.

twist.text: The Bantu expansion within Africa was another massive migration, reshaping the continent's genetics 3,000 years ago.

climax.text: Human migration was never a simple arrow. It was a web of movements, returns, and re-mixings.

punchline.text: People kept leaving, coming back, and mixing.

quiz.question: How did Neanderthal DNA reach some African populations?
options: Eurasian populations carrying Neanderthal DNA migrated back into Africa
